messages.subject: Re: Problem with run DEC model
messages.body_plain:
Hi again Nick

I followed your suggestions to my datasets, but the same error message is still appearing. I send you my files with the changes you recommended. I hope you can help me.

Thank you so much!

El lunes, 17 de junio de 2019, 19:50:43 (UTC-5), carlos jimenez escribió:
> Hi Nick
>
> I'm trying to run a DEC model in BioGeoBEARS but when the loop run appears the next message:
>
> STOP ERROR #3 in bears_optim_run(). Test calculation of the likelihood with calc_loglike_for_optim_stratified() returned LnL=-1e+50, which is not a valid starting likelihood. Probably, you have an overly constrained analysis and have thus made your data impossible. For example, if your tips had ranges A and B, but you disallowed the state AB, then your data would be impossible under DEC, because AB is a required intermediate state. Try removing some of the areas allowed/area adjacency/manual states list constraints.  You can also try changing manual dispersal multipliers from 0 to some small value (e.g. 0.00001) -- note that this can works on dispersal multiplers, but NOT on area constraints, which have to be 0 or 1.  Have a CAREFUL THINK about what you are doing and why you think the list of ranges should be so constrained - do you actually have a good argument for your constraints?
>
> I changed the probability in the dispersal file from 0 to 0.00001 but the same message continue appearing. I attach my files for this analysis, I hope that you can help me.
>
> Thank you for your help!
> _________________________
> Carlos Jiménez-Rivillas
>

messages.subject: improving plotting in BioGeoBEARS
messages.body_plain:
A question about improving plotting in BioGeoBEARS:

XXX writes:
>
> Beside that, I'm having trouble to edit the PDF file to make the tree/figure more legible (I pasted below a screenshot from what I have).
>
> My tip labels and even the tree nodes/branches are kind of heaped. I guess must have a way to set a better spacing for this features..
> But my R skills are limited yet.. Do you know if there are tutorial to deal with this? Or the best way is to go to an image edition?
>
> Thanks again for all your comments.
>
> Best,
XXX

Answer:

Hi -- to improve the PDF:

0. Use single-letter codes for all areas

1. Play with the height and width arguments of the pdf() command

2. Play with these arguments -- cex means "character expansion" in R:
label.offset=0.45, tipcex=0.7, statecex=0.7, splitcex=0.6, titlecex=0.8, plotsplits=TRUE

3. Once you get it close, open the PDF in Adobe Illustrator or the similar free program, Inkscape I think, to do final tweaks for publication.

Cheers!
Nick

messages.body_plain:
Hi - the error means you are getting NAs in the calculations, which can come from having probability-zero of the data due to a combination of the dispersal constraints and the model.  So, first try: changing your 0s to 0.01 in the dispersal multipliers file, DIVALIKE models.

Note: the distances file, where the base dispersal probability is multiplied by distance^x,  is also irrelevant if you just have a 2-area system, it is only doing something useful if  you have differences in distances between multiple areas. Trying to estimate both x & the dispersal rate probably won't work very well as with only 1 distance between 2 areas, the optimizer can't tell whether it should change x or dispersal -- this is called an "identifiability" problem.

Cheers!
Nick

messages.body_plain:
Dear Dr. Matzke,

Thank you for accepting me in this group.

I am currently trying to learn how to use the package and is piecing together the workflow and how to obtain the files it works with.

To my understanding, a phylogeny/tree needs to be generated from another application (e.g. BEAST); and then a geography file in PHYLIP format.

I was hoping to find out if my current understanding is correct and more particularly if the geography file is something that can be encoded manually (based on absence/presence data) or should be generated in PHYLIP.

Thank you.

-Vhon

messages.subject: Re: [BioGeoBEARS] Working pipeline
messages.body_plain:
Hi!

Yes, you need a Newick file representing a dated phylogeny -- this can come from anywhere, but most commonly comes from a BEAST MCC summary tree.

(Technically, BEAST analysis -> ".trees" NEXUS file that is a sample of dated trees from the posterior distribution -> TreeAnnotator used to summarize the posterior distribution with a Maximum Clade Credibility (MCC) tree in NEXUS format -> View the NEXUS MCC tree in FigTree, ladderize the tree view if desired, and save it out to a Newick file)

For the PHYLIP-format geography file, almost everyone just codes these by hand in a plain-text editor. You can use Excel or R or whatever to create the geography files if you have some technical skills.  PHYLIP is just the format, there is no way to use the PHYLIP program to make the geography files.

Here are text-file examples of all the input files:
http://phylo.wikidot.com/biogeobears#links_to_files

View them in a good, plain-text editor, not an internet browser or Word:

Text files should be viewed/edited WITH A REAL PLAIN-TEXT EDITOR
http://phylo.wikidot.com/biogeobears#texteditors

Cheers!
Nick
